🇲🇽🏭 <u>Edomex 2027: Social Programs Up 7%, Zero New Debt, Zero New Taxes</u>

Governor Delfina Gómez sent a 433.8-billion-peso 2027 budget to the State of Mexico legislature: 231.3 billion, more than half, goes to social welfare, with an extra 1.4 billion for social programs (+7%) and 2.3 billion more for health. No new taxes, no tax hikes, the vehicle-tax subsidy stays, and for the fourth straight year the state takes on no new public debt. Mexico's most populous state spent decades under the PRI as a piggy bank for the Atlacomulco group.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>Segob: Senior Pension Is a Constitutional Right, "Not for Some and Not for Others"</u>

After CEPAL and the World Bank credited Mexico's universal senior pension with cutting poverty and inequality, Interior Secretary Rosa Icela Rodríguez pointed to who it reaches most: older women who spent their lives caring for children and grandchildren with no formal pension. "These are rights, they are in the Constitution, and they are not for some and not for others."

🇲🇽🇨🇺 <u>Mexico and Cuba Restart Parliamentary Summit After Three-Year Freeze</u>

Mexico's Senate hosts the XVIII Mexico-Cuba Interparliamentary Meeting today and tomorrow, the first in three years. Senate president Higinio Martínez says health, economy, science, culture and sport are on the table, with a joint declaration expected. Cuban ambassador Eugenio Martínez Enríquez: "Mexico and Cuba are two sister countries, united."

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Supreme Court Slams the Door on Grupo México: 18.4M Peso Fine Stands</u>

Mexico's Supreme Court threw out Buenavista del Cobre's last appeal against an 18.4-million-peso Profepa fine. Germán Larrea's Sonora copper mine was allowed 540,000 tons of mining waste and dumped 613,218 in 2022-23. Chief Justice Hugo Aguilar dismissed the appeal without even sending it to the full court: the case "does not hold exceptional legal interest." Same mine, same company that spilled 40,000 m³ of acidified copper sulfate into the Sonora River in 2014, poisoning 271 km of riverbed and 22,000 people.

🇲🇽🛢️ <u>Mexico aims to import just 12% of its fuel by 2030</u>

Senate Energy Committee chair Beatriz Robles says SENER projects fuel imports falling to 12% of consumption by 2030, driven by the Olmeca refinery at Dos Bocas, Deer Park and the rehab of the six old refineries. El Financiero checked Pemex's own figures: gasoline imports averaged 598,200 barrels a day in 2018 and 325,400 in January–September 2026, down 45.7% in eight years. "We have the oranges and we import the juice," she said of refineries that had been running at 40% capacity.

🇲🇽🧒 <u>Mexico to spend 1.1 trillion pesos on children and teens in 2027</u>

Just over 1.102 trillion pesos goes to children and adolescents next year, according to Sipinna's Aurora Aguilar. The gap is real: of 12.2 million kids aged 0 to 5, 41.9% live in poverty and 56.9% lack social security. The 2026–2030 early-childhood strategy aims to cut chronic malnutrition from 14% to 7.5%, extreme poverty from 8.8% to 7.3%, and lift preschool attendance from 63.6% to 73% by 2030.

🇲🇽🔎 <u>Segob to searching mothers at the FGR sit-in: your protest is legitimate, let's talk</u>

Interior Secretary Rosa Icela Rodríguez said the sit-in relatives of the disappeared have held for days at the Attorney General's Office is legitimate and must be attended, and that "there can be no impunity." The heads of the National Search Commission and the Victims Commission have met the group in person. She said people are located every day, that search takes more of her ministry's time than anything else, and opened the 24/7 National Immediate Search Alert command center to the press. "We're not letting up."

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Morena runs its 2027 hopefuls through the Financial Intelligence Unit</u>

Morena president Ariadna Montiel told Contralínea the party is working with the UIF to block candidates whose wealth doesn't match their income. Files with criminal records plus UIF and SAT data were already delivered on the state coordinators picked for 2027, and the review covers anyone with a significant party post, not just candidates. "We have a commitment to the people that they be suitable, honest representatives." The opposition voted against the reform that created a vetting commission inside the INE.

🇲🇽💼 <u>SAT widens the simplified tax regime for small businesses in 2027</u>

Resico, the low-rate regime created in 2022, gets bigger in January. The income ceiling for individuals rises from 3.5 to 5 million pesos a year; for small companies, from 35 to 50 million. Income tax stays at 1% to 2.5%. The SAT says the regime has grown 130% since launch, with about 40,000 individuals and 1,400 companies signing up every week. Those who were pushed out can return if they're under the limit and up to date.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>Sheinbaum closes APEC: ten deals with China, no trade treaty, T-MEC on track</u>

"We brought the representation of the people." Sheinbaum wrapped up her China trip calling it very productive: about ten memorandums of understanding and preliminary cooperation agreements signed with Beijing on economy, environment, energy, health, science and technology. She ruled out any trade treaty with China and said the relationship won't affect ties with the US, where the T-MEC review could close in December.
